key_insight: Computer-vision-informed void nucleation makes shock damage predictions sensitive to grain-scale microstructure, with representative microstructures needed to reproduce measured free-surface velocity.
engineering_relevance: The model supports microstructure-aware prediction of spallation in tantalum under high-rate plate-impact loading.
method: Predict a void-nucleation susceptibility field from grain orientations and grain-boundary energy.
Combine susceptibility with a local maximum-principal-stress barrier in a continuum damage model.
Couple damage to crystal plasticity in a Lagrangian shock simulation with selectively resolved microstructure.
evidence_signal: Calibrated at 196 m/s flyer velocity, the model reproduced key experimental free-surface-velocity features and transferred to 214 m/s without parameter changes, with some late-time ringing deviations.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported tantalum impact cases, and predictions depend on using representative microstructures.
paper_title: A mesoscale damage model for void nucleation and growth in shock loaded microstructure informed by computer vision
